newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha up in dull trade, LSWR sentiment firm.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha up in dull trade, LSWR sentiment firm.

text.p: Naphtha prices were notionally higher on Tuesday in a market devoid of participants due to an open-spec naphtha conference in Tokyo, traders said.
"There's just nothing going on in the market," one naphtha broker said.
Trading is expected to revive on Wednesday as the two-day conference ended on Tuesday.
In low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) trading, Indonesia's initial allocation for July lifting was rumoured to total about 2.3 million barrels, setting bullish sentiment in the spot market.
However, some fuel oil traders said about 400,000 to 500,000 barrels of Indonesian cargoes were likely to be rolled over from June, in addition to the initial July allocation.
Indonesia's state-owned oil concern Pertamina initially allocated 3.1 million barrels of LSWR for June and 3.7 to 3.9 million barrels for May, traders said.
Open-spec naphtha for second-half August was nominally assessed at $198.50/200.00 per tonne, up from late Monday's $197.50/199.00.
